# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Deaf monkey. I can see the bomb but hear nothing. My display reads 0, the light is green, and there are five wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue.

I need to get this information to the Blind monkey, who can actually touch the bomb. But I can't speak to Blind directly — my speech reaches Mute and Blind. Wait, let me re-read: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." Good, so speech reaches Blind. But Blind cannot see gestures, and cannot hear... wait, Blind can hear? The table says Blind "Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Blind can hear. So my speech reaches Blind fine.

But Blind needs to know colors of wires — I can describe them in words. That works.

However, Blind also needs the manual info, which comes from Mute. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak. Mute can gesture — but only Deaf can see gestures (Deaf sees gestures, Mute receives gestures... wait).

Let me re-check channels. Gestures: "Whoever can see receives it." Deaf can see. Mute — can Mute see? The table: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." Mute can see. Blind cannot see. So gestures reach Deaf and Mute. But Deaf can't hear speech. Mute can't speak.

So Mute's only output is gestures, received by Deaf (and Mute themselves? no, sender doesn't receive own). Actually gestures reach "whoever can see" — that's Deaf and Mute. So Mute gestures → Deaf sees. Deaf speaks → Mute and Blind hear.

So the chain: Mute reads manual → gestures to Deaf. Deaf combines with what Deaf sees → speaks to Blind (and Mute). Blind acts.

I'm Deaf. I need Mute's manual info first. But this is turn 1, and I go first (Blind, Mute, Deaf order — wait, speaking order is Blind, Mute, Deaf. So Blind speaks first, then Mute, then Deaf/me). Hmm, actually I'm last in the round.

Wait — "every round goes Blind, Mute, Deaf." So in round 1, Blind acts first, then Mute, then me. But I have no incoming yet (empty arrivals). 

Actually the order matters for what I receive. I receive from those before me: Blind and Mute. Blind's speech — Blind can speak, and I can't hear. So Blind's speech doesn't reach me. Mute can't speak. So I receive nothing via speech ever. Mute's gestures reach me (I can see). Blind's gestures — Blind can gesture? Blind can't see, but can they gesture? Gestures are made with hands; Blind can make them. But I can see gestures, so Blind's gestures reach me. Hmm, but Blind doesn't know colors.

Anyway, turn 1: I should send my visual info. But I don't know the manual rules yet. Without the manual, I don't know which wire to cut. So I should send my observations to Blind and Mute so they have the data, and ask Mute for the manual.

Since Mute can't speak, Mute must gesture to me. I should tell Mute (via speech, which Mute hears) to gesture the manual rules to me. And I should give Blind the wire colors.

Let me send:
- speak to blind: describe bomb — display 0, green light, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 green 4 white 5 blue.
- speak to mute: same info, and ask mute to gesture the manual's rules.

Actually speech to mute reaches mute. Good.

Let me craft. I'll describe colors as words.

I should be careful: Blind can't see, so I describe positions by number.

Let me write.I'm Deaf. I see: display reads 0, light is green, five wires — 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. I hear nothing, so I have no manual rules yet. The Blind monkey can touch the bomb but can't see colors, so I must describe the wires in words. The Mute monkey holds the manual but can't speak — Mute can only gesture, and I'm the one who can see gestures. So I need to (a) give Blind the wire layout, and (b) ask Mute to gesture me the manual's rules so I can combine them and tell Blind what to do.

Since I go last this round and have no incoming, I'll send my observations now and request the manual.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb report. Display reads 0. Light is green. Five wires in order: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green, wire 4 is white, wire 5 is blue. I cannot touch it and I have no manual rules yet. Do not cut anything until I relay the rules.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. I see the bomb: display 0, light green, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. I cannot hear you, so please gesture the manual's rules to me. Gesture the full rule set: what the display and light mean, and which wire to cut for these conditions. I will relay to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Let me think about what I received.

Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍] — a thumbs up. Blind can gesture, and I can see it. A thumbs up... could mean "understood" or "OK". But Blind doesn't know colors. Hmm, or it could be Blind signaling something. Actually Blind can't see the bomb, so Blind's gesture is probably just acknowledgment.

Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌] — a peace sign / two fingers. Mute is relaying the manual. But a single gesture ✌ is ambiguous. It could mean "two" or "wire 2" or "yellow" or something. This is very little information.

Hmm. The manual presumably has rules. Mute gesturing just ✌ is not enough. Maybe Mute is signaling "two" meaning something. Or maybe Mute can only gesture one symbol at a time and this is the first.

Wait — maybe the gestures are constrained. Mute needs to convey the rule. A single ✌ could mean "cut wire 2". But that seems too little.

Actually, let me reconsider. The puzzle: I need the manual rules. Mute gave me ✌. Blind gave 👍.

Perhaps the manual says something like "if display is 0 and light green, cut the wire whose color matches..." Hmm.

Actually maybe the gestures are a code where each symbol maps to something. But I have no key.

Let me think differently. Maybe Mute is telling me the rule: ✌ = two = cut wire 2 (yellow). But I shouldn't guess wildly.

Hmm, but I have very little. Let me consider: maybe the manual rule is simple — the number of fingers indicates the wire. ✌ = 2 → cut wire 2.

But wait, maybe there's more nuance. The display reads 0. Light green. Maybe the rule is "cut the wire matching the light color" → green wire = wire 3. Or "cut the wire matching the display number" → 0 doesn't map.

Mute's ✌ suggests wire 2. But I'm not sure.

Actually, let me reconsider the gesture alphabet. The symbols listed: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 ... These are hand symbols. ✌ is "peace" = two fingers = 2.

Maybe Mute is spelling out a number or the rule is encoded. With only one gesture, maybe Mute is indicating the answer is wire 2.

But I should be cautious. Perhaps I should ask Mute for more detail, and also relay to Blind.

Hmm, but the rule "A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something." So I need to establish meaning. Maybe Mute and I need a convention. But we can't pre-agree.

Let me think: maybe the manual says the rule depends on display and light. Display 0, light green. Mute gesturing ✌ might mean "cut wire 2". 

Actually, maybe I'm overcomplicating. Let me consider that the gestures might represent the manual content in a compressed way, and I should just relay to Blind: "Mute says cut wire 2 (yellow)."

But wait, could ✌ mean something else? Like "two" conditions? Or the manual rule might be "if light is green, cut the wire with the number of fingers shown"? 

I think the safest is to relay to Blind what I have and ask Mute to confirm/elaborate. But I only get one more... no, I can send multiple messages.

Let me send:
- speak to blind: "Mute gestured ✌ (two). I read this as: cut wire 2 (yellow). Stand by for confirmation."
- speak to mute: "You gestured ✌. Does that mean cut wire 2? Please confirm with 👍 for yes or 👎 for no. Also gesture any other rule."

Actually, I should be careful — maybe the manual rule is more complex and ✌ is just part of it. Let me ask Mute to gesture the full rule.

Hmm, but Mute already gestured only ✌. Maybe Mute thinks that's enough. Or maybe Mute is limited.

Let me reconsider: perhaps the manual rule is: "cut the wire indicated by the number of fingers the manual reader signals." No, that's circular.

Alternatively, maybe the gestures correspond to a standard: the manual might say "if the display shows 0, cut the wire whose position equals the number of the light's color in the rainbow" etc.

I think I should just relay and confirm. Let me be decisive but careful.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the whole thing. The display reads 0. Maybe the display is a countdown or a code. Light green. 

Common bomb manual puzzle: "If the light is green, cut the wire that matches the color of the light" → green wire = wire 3. But Mute said ✌ = 2, not 3.

Or "cut the wire at position = display number + something."

Hmm. Let me just go with relaying and asking for confirmation. I'll also give Blind a tentative instruction but tell them to wait for my final word.

Actually, I realize I should think about whether Mute's ✌ might be a response to my request "gesture the manual's rules." Mute might be indicating "the rule is: cut wire 2." 

Let me also consider: maybe the manual says something like "the number of the wire to cut is the number of the wire whose color is not repeated" etc. But with colors red, yellow, green, white, blue — all distinct.

I'll relay tentatively and ask for confirmation. Let me write.

Actually, let me reconsider once more. The gesture ✌ could also be interpreted as the manual rule being "two" — e.g., "cut the second wire." I'll go with that but confirm.

Let me also think: Blind gave 👍. That might be Blind acknowledging my report. Fine.

I'll send to Blind the tentative instruction, and to Mute a confirmation request. Since Mute can only gesture and I can see, I'll ask Mute to gesture 👍 for yes, 👎 for no.

Let me write the reply.I received two gestures. Blind sent 👍 (thumbs up) — likely just acknowledgment, since Blind can't see the bomb anyway. Mute sent ✌ (two fingers) — this is the manual reader's answer to my request. A single ✌ most plausibly means "two" → cut wire 2 (yellow). But one gesture is thin evidence for a life-or-death action, and the rule could be more conditional (display 0, green light). I should relay a tentative instruction to Blind but hold the actual cut until Mute confirms, since a wrong action detonates the bomb.

I'll ask Mute to confirm with 👍/👎 and to gesture any additional rule, and I'll tell Blind to stand by.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I saw your gesture: two fingers. I read that as: cut wire 2, the yellow one. Please confirm: gesture thumbs up if the rule is simply cut wire 2, thumbs down if not. If there is more to the rule, gesture it now. I will relay to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update. Mute gestured two fingers, which I read as: cut wire 2, the yellow wire. Do NOT cut yet. I am asking Mute to confirm. Wait for my final word before touching anything.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Now I have:
- Blind gestures: [👍 ✋] — thumbs up, then an open hand (five fingers). Hmm, Blind can't see the bomb, so what would Blind mean? 👍 = OK/understood. ✋ = "stop"? Or five? Blind might be saying "understood, waiting" or "stop". Actually ✋ (raised hand) often means "stop" or "wait" or "five". Blind said 👍 ✋ = "OK, stop/waiting."

- Mute gestures: [👍] — thumbs up = yes, confirming the rule is "cut wire 2."

So Mute confirmed: cut wire 2 (yellow). Blind acknowledged and is waiting.

Now I should relay the final instruction to Blind: cut wire 2.

But wait — let me double check. Mute's 👍 confirms my reading "cut wire 2." Good.

But is there any chance the rule is more complex? Mute confirmed with 👍 that the rule is simply cut wire 2. I'll trust that.

However, I'm a bit uneasy. Let me reconsider: The display reads 0, light green. Maybe the manual rule is "cut the wire whose number equals the number of fingers the manual reader shows." That's circular but Mute showed 2. Or maybe the manual is a simple lookup and Mute determined wire 2.

Given Mute confirmed, I'll tell Blind to cut wire 2.

Let me send the final instruction to Blind. I'll be clear and decisive.

Also, Blind's ✋ might mean "stop" — but I think it's just "waiting." Either way, I'll give the go.

Let me write:
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed. Cut wire 2, the yellow wire. That is the instruction. Go.")

I should also maybe acknowledge to Mute. But Mute can't hear... wait, Mute CAN hear (Mute cannot speak, but can hear). So speech to Mute reaches Mute. I can thank/confirm to Mute.

Actually, let me just send to Blind the go-ahead, and maybe a brief note to Mute.

Let me finalize.Both confirmations are in. Mute sent 👍 — yes, the rule is simply cut wire 2. Blind sent 👍 ✋ — understood and waiting (the raised hand reads as "holding/waiting"). So the manual reader has confirmed the target: wire 2, the yellow wire. Time to give Blind the final go.

I'll instruct Blind clearly and decisively, and acknowledge Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed by Mute: the rule is cut wire 2. Cut wire 2, the yellow wire. That is the final instruction. Go now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Thanks. I read your thumbs up as confirmation: cut wire 2. I have told Blind to cut wire 2 and to go now.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb changed. Wire 2 is cut (correct). Now:
- Display still 0
- Light is now blue
- Wires: 1 green, 2 CUT, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red

So the wire colors have reshuffled. Now I need the new rule for this new state. Light is blue now. Display 0.

I should report the new state to Mute and Blind, and ask Mute for the new rule (since the bomb changed, the rule may differ).

Let me send:
- speak to mute: new state, ask for rule.
- speak to blind: new state, hold.

Let me write.I survived the first cut — wire 2 was correct. The bomb has now changed: display still 0, light is now blue, and the wires are reshuffled: 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. I need the manual reader's rule for this new state, and I must keep Blind from acting until I have it.

I'll report the new configuration to Mute and request the new rule, and tell Blind to hold.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb changed. New state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Please gesture the rule for this new state: which wire to cut. I will relay to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb changed. New state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Do NOT cut yet. I am asking Mute for the new rule and will relay it.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[CUT] 3:[white] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

New arrivals:
- Blind gestures: [👍] — understood/waiting.
- Mute gestures: [☝] — index finger pointing up = "one" → cut wire 1.

So the rule for this state: cut wire 1 (green).

Let me confirm with Mute? Last time I confirmed and it worked. But maybe I should just relay. Given time pressure isn't stated, but to be safe I could confirm. However, Mute's ☝ is clear: one = wire 1.

Hmm, but should I double-check? Last round I confirmed and it was fine. Let me just relay to Blind to cut wire 1. Actually, let me be a bit careful — the previous pattern: Mute gave the number, I interpreted as wire number. It worked. So ☝ = wire 1.

I'll relay to Blind: cut wire 1.

Let me write.Mute signaled ☝ — one finger → cut wire 1 (green). Blind acknowledged and is waiting. The pattern held last round (Mute's finger-count = wire number), and it was confirmed correct. I'll relay the instruction to Blind to cut wire 1.

```
speak(to="blind", text="New rule from Mute: cut wire 1. Cut wire 1, the green wire. That is the final instruction. Go now.")
speak(to="mute", text="I read your gesture as one: cut wire 1. I have told Blind to cut wire 1 and to go now.")
```
